items.title: Chrona 01: look-and-feel inventory of the legacy time-tracking-application (screens, layout, styles, interactions)
items.description: Build order: Chrona is first (user decision 2026-10-08). The user expects Chrona to be reconstructed rather than migrated: KEEP the look and feel, rebuild the code to all current standards with no compromises. Read-only source: kemiller2002/time-tracking-application (do not modify). Inventory every screen in static-ui-screens/ (today, start, stop, manual-entry, activity, correction, split, merge, remove, restore, evidence, review, month, more, settings, sign-in, states, index) and the live web/ client (index.html, styles.css, main.js, dom-bindings.js, service worker, manifest). Record layout, navigation, typography, colour and spacing tokens, components, interaction patterns, keyboard and mobile behaviour, and offline cues, plus docs/UI-*.md (architecture, components, state model, accessibility, offline behaviour, visual review). Map each style to a Forma equivalent or a documented gap. Output: docs/legacy/look-and-feel-inventory.md with screenshots. Requirements: CHX-011, CHX-012, CHX-320, CHX-330. No dependencies.

items.title: Chrona 02: decide reconstruction versus migration, record legacy data status and rewrite the charter for the time-tracking product (CHX-011, CHX-012, CHX-300, CHX-310)
items.description: Depends on WI-0026. Record the decision (the user expects reconstruction, not migration) as a Praxis decision record. Reconcile the expansion's restatement against the legacy docs/DOMAIN-REQUIREMENTS.md in time-tracking-application (an open item in the gap analysis). Record the legacy data status: kemiller2002/time-tracking-data holds an append-only JSON event ledger (ledger/YYYY/MM/activities, evidence-links, derived indexes, integrity manifests), and at 2026-10-08 it contains only DEMO records (ACT-20260802-DEMO-*, EVL-20260802-DEMO-001). No production data needs migrating today. If real records appear, an import is a Chrona application-level migration on top of Arca's migration workflow (ARCA OQ-ARCA-005). Cover rename and source compatibility (CHX-310). Replace the generic PROJECT-CHARTER.md and context/CURRENT-STATE.md with the actual time-tracking product (CHX-011).

items.title: Chrona 03: configurable data location and Chrona-owned namespace with organization manifests (CHX-DATALOC-001, CHX-024..027)
items.description: Depends on arca slice 2 (data location, ARCA-LOC) and arca slice 3 (record format, ARCA-REC) (data location and record format). New requirement CHX-DATALOC-001 (docs/requirements/CHRONA-DATA-LOCATION.md, user decision 2026-10-08): the data repository is configured per deployment and never hard-coded; Chrona creates and owns its namespace and never assumes it is the only application in the repository; Chrona's data must be separable under different permissions from other applications (for example Summa), which means deploying against its own repository, because GitHub permissions are per repository; no at-rest encryption for now. Also: organization folders with immutable OrganizationIds, the organization manifest (CHX-026), and public-repository refusal for production (CHX-027).

items.title: Chrona 04: GitHub sign-in through Fides and token safety (CHX-022, CHX-023)
items.description: Depends on fides slice 7 (WASM client and Arca token provider, FID-CLI) (WASM client and Arca token provider) and arca slice 5 (token-provider port, ARCA-AUTH) (token-provider port). Sign in through Fides (GitHub only for now). Resolve the identity from GitHub, never a typed username. Tokens never reach records, integration messages, telemetry, logs, exports or artifacts. Disconnect/clear token is supported, and session-only retention is the default.

items.title: Chrona 05: actors, membership and capability-based authorization (CHX-030, CHX-260 remainder)
items.description: Depends on WI-0029. Human/Agent/Service/Integration principals, membership in several organizations, and capability-based authorization (RecordOwnTime ... PublishBillableTime) separate from GitHub authentication. Reference-data changes need admin capabilities. Authorization diagnostics use stable CHRONA.* codes.

items.title: Chrona 06: reference data on Arca - authoritative reference records, their storage and administration across devices (CHX-040 remainder, CHX-063 remainder)
items.description: Depends on WI-0028. The pure catalogue, archive semantics, assignment rules and billing references were built in memory by WI-0045; this item makes reference data authoritative records stored through Arca (organization-scoped, shared across devices and people) and wires the CHX-063 remainder (Summa's InvoicedExternally report and ReadyForPublication staging). Also the CHX-030 remainder: organization rosters (Access.Roster) stored as records beside the reference data, members admitted and capabilities granted or revoked across devices by those who hold ManageOrganizationSettings, and choosing the organization to work in when a person belongs to several.

items.title: Chrona 07: authoritative storage on Arca - partitioned layout, repository concurrency, integrity and manual edits (CHX-021, CHX-210, CHX-220, CHX-380, CHX-390, CHX-410, CHX-240 remainder, CHX-050 persistence)
items.description: Depends on WI-0028, WI-0030, arca slice 6 (GitHub adapter, ARCA-API/OUT) (GitHub adapter) and arca slice 8 (integrity, ARCA-INT) (integrity). Persist Chrona.Domain records through Arca: deterministic partitioned paths (organization/actor/year-month), bounded reads and writes, one operation as one commit, repository-state optimistic concurrency with reload, revalidation and surfaced semantic conflicts (a clean Git merge is not proof), validation of everything loaded, detection of manual edits, and an API-efficient today view. Covers scenarios 10, 31 and 32 end to end. Also the remaining evidence-reference fields (source, notes) of CHX-240. Includes persisting the full CHX-050 activity record. Also the WI-0028 remainders (CHX-024..027): read the deployment configuration and drive Storage.initializeApplication/initializeOrganization/openNamespace and Organization.read/renameOrganization through Arca's GitHub adapter from the Limen engine, store activities in each organization's folder (chrona/datasets/<OrganizationId>, its own repository when configured), and detect repository visibility from GitHub (Arca repository identity) before initializing production data. The pure persistence core (record codec, partitioned layout, change sets, integrity on load, manual-edit review, reload-and-rerun) is WI-0051; this item drives it through Arca's GitHub adapter from the Limen engine and covers the remaining API-efficiency (conditional requests, cached derived indexes, paging, rate limits, backoff) and integrity checks (receipts, publications). Token safety on the storage path (CHX-023 remainder): the GitHub adapter gets its token only from Fides' token provider (Identity.TokenProvider), reports a 401 to Fides, and no token reaches a commit, record, log or fault. Also the CHX-260 remainder of the stable diagnostics: an unresolved semantic merge conflict after reload (and, with their own items, the submitted-period restriction in WI-0036, the concurrent timer conflict in WI-0033 and the unsupported integration contract in WI-0037).

items.title: Chrona 08: offline use, persisted timer and sync reconciliation (CHX-101, CHX-102, CHX-105, CHX-200, CHX-230)
items.description: Depends on WI-0032 and arca slice 9 (offline queue, ARCA-OFF) (offline queue). The timer and manual entry work offline. The active timer survives refresh and restart, and recovery runs at startup. Sync state is visible. Reconnection reconciles idempotently. Conflicts become visible obligations. Startup reconciliation is non-blocking, resumable and paged. Scenarios 4, 33 and 34.

items.description: The storage-independent part of WI-0036: daily, weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly and monthly periods with a configurable week start, time zone, submission expectation and approval requirement; period summaries with exact, billable, non-billable and unclassified time, submission and approval state and outstanding obligations; a period panel on Today. items.title: Chrona 14a: search, reports and deterministic export in memory, printable through Folio (CHX-270, CHX-280, CHX-290, CHX-005)
items.description: The in-memory part of WI-0039: filters and text search over the session's records, reports by day, project, activity type and tag that keep exact and billable time apart, deterministic CSV and JSON exports that name the organization, generation time, range, schema version, filters and duration semantics, copied through Limen's clipboard effect, and a printable Folio document. Derived, rebuildable indexes on Arca stay with WI-0039 and WI-0034.

items.title: Chrona 13a: observation processing in the pure domain - candidates, dispositions (pending, accepted, accepted with changes, rejected, duplicate, needs attention), source auto-accept policy, deduplication and receipts (CHX-190, CHX-120 import path, CHX-250 import audit; scenarios 25-30)
items.description: The storage-independent part of WI-0038, per coordinator direction 2026-10-08. TimeObservation to TimeCandidate to ProcessingReceipt as pure rules: review by default unless a source policy allows auto-accept, rejected observations preserved with reason, invalid payloads distinguishable from rejected ones, deduplication by source and observation id and by content, receipts never issued before the candidate decision exists (receipt repair), accepted activities keep source system, observation id, work item, external URL and ingestion time, imports pass the same overlap and classification rules and are audited. Inbox storage, the receiver-owned Chrona.Integration contract assembly and reconciliation stay with WI-0038 and WI-0037.

items.title: Chrona 07a: activity records on Arca - record codec, partitioned layout, change sets and integrity on load (CHX-220, CHX-390, CHX-410, CHX-050 persistence)
items.description: Split from WI-0032 (storage-free in the sense that it needs no GitHub or Fides): the pure persistence core on Arca.Core, tested against Arca's in-memory provider. The activity record codec (closed, versioned chrona.activity records), deterministic partitioned paths (organization folder / actor / year / month, stable ids, bounded month reads for the today view), change sets (one ledger command is one operation; a retimed activity that changes month moves in the same commit; every update and delete carries the revision last read), integrity on load (expansion 39: invalid JSON, schema, unsupported versions, misplaced records, duplicate ids, impossible revisions, overlapping recorded time, broken split/merge lineage; corruption is reported, never ignored), manual-edit detection from Arca commit history (41), and reload-and-revalidate after a conflict so independent changes are preserved and semantic conflicts surface (21). WI-0032 then drives this through Arca's GitHub adapter from the Limen engine.

items.title: Chrona 04b: real end-to-end sign-in against a deployed Fides exchange and GitHub App (CHX-022 remainder)
items.description: Waits on the user's deployment: Fides is not deployed anywhere yet (no AWS account, domain or GitHub App). When a Fides exchange is hosted (Fides docs/hosting/AWS.md) with Chrona registered (origin and redirect URI) and a GitHub App exists, write that deployment's chrona.deployment.json (docs/deployment-configuration.md), sign in with a real GitHub account, check the identity Chrona shows is GitHub's, that the token is kept as chosen and revoked on sign-out, that a refresh after eight hours works, and that the exchange's CORS allows exactly the deployment's origin. WI-0029 built and tested all of it against a fake exchange and GitHub; this is the check against the real ones.
